entities.label: Ghesh
entities.basis: Named in the session transcript; identity corroborated by the linked note.
entities.session_overview: Kenzo gambles with Ghesh, buys his discretion and guidance, races him on the way to Megren, and pays him after the introduction.

entities.label: Megren
entities.basis: Named in the session transcript; identity corroborated by the linked note.
entities.session_overview: Megren tells Kenzo she traded the jade fragment to Ra’ghemdros, describes the dragon’s dangerous lair, and passes on rumors of an elder despite fearing reprisals.

entities.label: Ra'ghemdros
entities.basis: Named in the session transcript; identity corroborated by the linked note.
entities.session_overview: The party learns that Ra’ghemdros holds the jade, rules the dragonets through fear and rewards, and is Cha’mutte’s daughter, then debates negotiation, theft, or fighting her.

entities.label: Dimitaur
entities.basis: Named in the session transcript; identity corroborated by the linked note.
entities.session_overview: After hearing rumors, locating and scrying the elder, the party bypasses Dimitaur’s trap and earns a conversation about Rai, Ra’ghemdros, Drankor, and Apollyon.

entities.label: Rai
entities.basis: Named in the session transcript; identity corroborated by the linked note.
entities.session_overview: The party uses its connection to Rai to seek the elder’s help and learns from Dimitaur about Rai’s disappearance and failed attempt to heal the land.

entities.label: Cha'mutte
entities.basis: Named in the session transcript; identity corroborated by the linked note.
entities.session_overview: The party connects Cha’mutte to the plague and learns from Dimitaur that Ra’ghemdros is his daughter and may still carry out an assigned task.

entities.label: Apollyon
entities.basis: Named in the session transcript; identity corroborated by the linked note.
entities.session_overview: Apollyon’s impending escape drives the party’s search for the jade, questions for Dimitaur, and debate over the guarded forge and possible alliances.

entities.label: Hobgoblin wizard in the mirror
entities.basis: Named in the session transcript; identity corroborated by the linked note.
entities.session_overview: During the Dimitaur conversation, the party considers consulting the imprisoned hobgoblin wizard as a potential ally against Cha’mutte’s daughter.

entities.label: Zadar
entities.basis: Named individual and specific source of Megren’s hearsay, u2516–u2627; not met by the party.
entities.session_overview: Megren cites Zadar’s account of an acid pool associated with dragonets who supposedly sought the rumored elder.

entities.label: Memorial forest
entities.basis: The DM explicitly establishes one collective consciousness at u4278–u4282 and u4422–u4425, speaking through the tree; keep one distinct entity, not one record per tree.
entities.session_overview: Kenzo communes with the forest about its memorials, isolation, and lost pilgrims, then honors its memories in his staff.

entities.label: Elven quartermaster remembered in the memorial
entities.basis: A specific individual’s memories are selected by the memorial at u4031–u4075; the written name is not transcribed.
entities.session_overview: Delwath sees a dead elf’s life as a quartermaster and their death in battle through the memorial.

entities.label: Rai’s jade hand fragments
entities.note: Campaigns/Dunmari Frontier Campaign/Treasure/Jade Piece of Rai's Hand.md
entities.basis: One quest collection with explicitly differentiated parts: four already held versus the remaining fragment reported with the dragon; no acquisition of the fifth occurs here.
entities.session_overview: The party learns Megren gave the sought fifth fragment to Ra’ghemdros, weighs how to recover it, and shows Dimitaur the four fragments already held in Kenzo’s staff.

entities.label: Staff of the Forest Soul
entities.note: Campaigns/Dunmari Frontier Campaign/Treasure/Staff of the Forest Soul.md
entities.basis: The transcript explicitly places Kenzo’s staff in the communion and jade reveal; canonical note resolves its identity only.
entities.session_overview: Kenzo uses his staff while communing with the memorial forest, seeks an image to preserve in it, and reveals its concealed jade fragments to Dimitaur.

entities.label: Gold circlet with four alexandrite gems
entities.basis: A specific gold circlet from Grimbaskal’s hoard is selected at u1614; the party negotiates its transfer and pays at u2657–u2663. Do not identify it with another named magic circlet.
entities.session_overview: Kenzo offers the circlet for Ghesh’s secrecy and guidance, then pays it over after the introduction to Megren.

entities.label: Mirror of Soul Trapping

entities.label: Apollyon’s phylactery
entities.basis: A specific central quest object discussed at u5152–u5193 and u5330–u5335; its form and location are not established here.
entities.session_overview: The party hopes completing Rai’s jade hand will reveal the phylactery’s location and questions Dimitaur about finding and destroying it.

review_notes: Selection: 21 narrative beats, fifth-highest raw count among 34 available Dunmari beat files (110:46, 109:33, 136:32, 139:23, 108:21). Chosen for sustained multi-NPC conversations rather than mostly combat or postgame discussion. All four core PCs are listed in the session note and speak in this transcript: Kenzo, Wellby, Delwath and Seeker.

Seventeen scenes follow actual movement and rest boundaries. The 21 editorial beats are supporting evidence, not automatic interaction boundaries. Ghesh’s extended visit, Megren’s interview, the forest communion and Dimitaur’s temple conversation each stay together.

Dimitaur’s card distinguishes rumor, remote detection, a delivered message, scrying, and the later direct meeting. Source order includes a retrospective clarification of the scry during the rest, not an additional hour or second rest.

Name knowledge is explicit: the party guesses at the elder’s identity earlier, but his in-world introduction is u5068. Revaka is only discussed as the wizard in the mirror; she is not summoned or released in this recording.

Zadar’s account is hearsay through Megren, not an encounter or confirmed observation of the alleged victims. Ra’ghemdros is mentioned throughout, never actually encountered. Do not use Dimitaur’s imitation of the dragon as a direct quote from her.

The forest is one explicitly established speaking consciousness, retained as a distinctive entity. The selected dead quartermaster is one observed individual; exclude generic dragonet groups, the unintelligent messenger spirit, and crowds of dead souls.

Exclude incidental deity iconography, loot-provenance names, the DM’s background-history reminders about Omnis Pura and Orestes, and current-campaign PCs including absent Riswynn. Rai and Dimitaur were PCs/companions in another campaign but are NPC subjects here.
The session metadata ends May 19, but this transcript ends with plans for a long rest. Played interactions are dated May 18; no unseen morning encounter is invented.

Version 3 adds important-item cards and one dominant type per scene; existing scene boundaries, indexes, dates and NPC encounter ranges are preserved. Extra NPC quotes stay inside the same conversations.

The jade card is a collection, not a claim that the party has an intact hand: four fragments are already held and one is still sought. The staff is a separate object. The mirror is only discussed and the phylactery’s form is not established. Later canonical item histories and powers are not imported into the session.

Major NPC quotes now include three from Ghesh, two from Megren and four from Dimitaur, without adding NPC interaction records. The short source excerpt on the circlet is explicitly Delwath’s inventory description, not speech by the object or an NPC.

Scene types use dominant activity: the guided journey is travel, the memorial investigation and magical communion are exploration, and the temple exchange is conversation. Existing source boundaries are unchanged.
